continuity_scope: Dragon Ball, VIZ English manga Volume 1 paperback (6 May 2003; ISBN-13 978-1-56931-920-8; 192 pages; Teen) and its separately listed digital edition (2 November 2010; eISBN-13 978-1-4215-4575-2; 188 pages). This is a narrow official English Volume 1 metadata/preview pass, not a panel-by-panel reading.
work_or_witnesses: Dragon Ball, Vol. 1, VIZ English paperback edition
Dragon Ball, Vol. 1, VIZ English digital edition
VIZ official Dragon Ball franchise profile
Shueisha original Japanese Volume 1 listing, as a separate original-language witness boundary only
VIZ VIZBIG sales description, as publisher orientation only for the Monkey King/Journey to the West inspiration caution
coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic character directly named in the selected VIZ English Volume 1 premise: Goku/Son Goku and Bulma. Dragon Balls, dragon god, quest, equipment, unnamed later heroes, martial roles, techniques, peoples/species, locations, and generic categories remain terms or omissions.
omissions: All other named Volume 1 figures, later manga, Dragon Ball Z/Super material, transformations, species, martial techniques, opponents, settings, and outcomes are omitted because the narrow official description does not establish them claim by claim.
Anime series, films, games, guidebooks, merchandise, later manga, Dragon Ball Super, adaptations, Japanese wording, and collected editions are separate witnesses.

The young protagonist, Teen rating, and action-adventure framing do not establish particular child endangerment, fanservice/sexualization, nudity, violence, injury, or content events; none are inferred from uninspected pages.
Journey to the West/Monkey King is recorded only as publisher-stated inspiration context and never as an identity claim joining Goku with Sun Wukong or any source character.
uncertainties: The VIZ listing offers a free preview but no browser-readable page/panel text locator, so claims are limited to its official synopsis and bibliographic metadata.
VIZ's Volume 1 text uses both Goku and Son Goku; the Japanese Shueisha page uses 孫悟空/Goku. This is a name/translation witness boundary, not evidence for any later alias or identity.
The VIZ franchise material mentions later intergalactic battles, but those are outside this early Volume 1 scope.
The VIZBIG product's Monkey King wording describes a collection of Volumes 1-3; it is used only to caution about inspiration, not as character evidence for the selected Volume 1 witness.
evidence_basis: VIZ and Shueisha first-party product metadata only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, unofficial guide, uninspected panel, or long quotation is used.
